for_you_if: you love grand strategy despite technical hurdles
you already own previous entries in the series
you have patience for complex tactical battles
not_for_you_if: you will not tolerate random desktop crashes

Warhammer III is not a game.

The drums thunder, the banners rise, and the world stretches toward the horizon every road lead to another price tag. Every faction whispers, "Pay." Every lord declares, "Buy." Every dream of commanding a grand empire is carved away and sold back to you piece by piece. 

Every time you think, "That faction looks fun," it's another DLC.

"That Legendary Lord looks awesome." Another DLC.

"That campaign would be interesting." Another DLC.

It never ends. You buy the game, and before you've even settled in you're hit with a wall of locked factions, locked Legendary Lords, locked units, and locked content. Everywhere you look it's another reminder that what you bought wasn't the full game—it was the privilege of paying even more.

I bought the "Total War: Warhammer III Collection" bundle idiotically believing that it would unlock all of the content for the game. What a fool I was. CREATIVE ASSEMBLY and Games Workshop are greedy. How can you hope for a fair, clear sale from the greedy? What a grand and intoxicating innocence. How could I be so naive? There is no deal.

Buying the $85.22 bundle--on sale 55% off, by the way, $190.68 normally, at the time of writing (it WILL go higher as they churn out more DLC)--does not actually include all of the DLC for this game. But even if you did then fill in all of the gaps by buying the rest of this game's DLC, you would still be missing content, because guess what? Want to play even the most basic, straightforward factions in Warhammer, like, I don't know, the Empire? Well sorry, your only option for the Empire is some totally-not-a-vampire-chick--the actual Emperor Karl Franz is off limits, along with most other factions in their ENTIRETY--unless you also buy BOTH of their previous Total War: Warhammer games, AND the DLC for those games in order to ACTUALY actually unlock everything. I think, anyway. Maybe their is some secret extra DLC I'll find out the game is withholding from me later on, they've done it once before already, after all.

The way they're chopping up their game so they can sell the parts of it that were already in the previous game back to you piecemeal nearly rivals EA in it's brazen greed--the only thing that keeps it from being on par being the fact that if you already owned the the previous games and their DLC, then I guess you don't need to rebuy it.

Also, just to be crystal clear, abhorrent DLC practices aside, even if I had gotten the game and all of its DLC for free (and all of the previous games and their DLC too, since again you need that for all this game's content), I still wouldn't recommend the game on the basis of quality either. At its best, it's just fine. But generally it's worse than Total War: SHOGUN 2, a game in …
80% of the content is locked behind a paywall for a game i payed for.

when 85% of your game is paid dlc to the point where not even the starting "free" factions - which are only a fraction of the total themselves - have access to all their units and mechanics is insane. It doesn't matter how good the game is, I will never recommend this game to anyone. Not in this economy.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that loading times are lengthy, with portions of playtime spent waiting on loading screens.

citations.review_text:
This is review is coming from someone who has had no total war or warhammer fantasy experience prior to playing this game.

[h1]What I like[/h1]
I like this game quite a lot and recommend it if you are like me, the kind of person who wants to feel like a commander of both a nation and armies in battle. This game really brings out that power-fantasy.

The split between the turn-based campaign and real-time battles works very nice for me, as the decision making for your empire and your troops in battle are different, so having that explicit divide that you bounce back and forth between is nice.

The scale is very nice too. Battles are large and full of spectacle that makes every battle feel epic, while still being strategically deep enough (at least for me) that it's worth taking the time to understand battle strategy to win your fights.

I also like the world setting as well. I don't know everything about the warhammer fantasy lore but I can say that it's pretty big and broad, so the world never feels boring as you expand.

One more thing I like is how every campaign is always different and unique, as a result of AI decision making and random events, meaning that even playing the same faction will never result in the same experience.

[h1]What I dislike[/h1]
While I do love this game, there are a few things to keep in mind. If any of the following is a deal breaker, either get it on sale or avoid.

The loading times are long. If you have a low-end pc, while you can run it, loading the campaign map can take 2-3 minutes each time while loading battles can take 45 seconds to a minute. I upgraded my pc to have somewhat more decent specs as noted in my pc specs attached, and it can still take about 30-45 seconds to load the campaign, and 15-30 seconds to load battles.

The learning curve can be somewhat steep. I don't think it's hard to understand but there's just a lot to take in and remember. However, once you do, the game really opens up. Thankfully, there are many, MA…
I have 1k hours playing this game and half of them stuck in my loading screen. Gonna reach for 2k hours looking at my loading screen again.

citations.review_text:
The AI is bad, the siege mechanics are bad, and there are far too many DLCs. Some races are ridiculously overpowered when played by the player, while others feel completely broken when controlled by the AI. On top of that, the game becomes repetitive and boring after around 30 turns, with very little keeping the campaign engaging in the long run.

1/10 I will play again

Whilst I believe this game has huge potential to be a fun experience, the broken state of some of the core mechanics will ruin your enjoyment of the game. First and foremost one has to mention the broken ai and its tendency to run away as much as possible. Be prepared to run after armies that will sack one settlement  after the other, while also having enough movement left to still not be in range of your force chasing it.  Skaven, Dwarfs and Greenskins in particular will do this without there being any good reason for doing so, apart from just pissing off the player.

Regular battles can be somewhat enjoyable, apart from the aweful army compositions the enemy lords will often field.  Armies consisting of 10+ diffrent types of units are commonly the norm, making battles a mess and just overall uncinematic. The ai will try flanking you with 70% of its units, which leads to utterly unfun battles, where you just have to break open your formation and fight in small clusters.

Sieges are by far the worst they have ever been in a Total War game, with most player just autoresolving 90% of them. Major and minor settlement layouts are chokepoint desasters, with all strategic and tactical planning missing. Walls pose no obstacle for the attacker, while almost being a detrement to the defender. Most siege maps force the attacker to rush, since towers are able to hit units from the start.  Don´t bother with siege equiment or artillery, since almost every unit can batter down gates or just climb the walls.

And of course, last but not least, the DLC pricing is just absurd. Wanna play ANY of the new factions? Well be prepared to spend some serious cash. Wanna get acces to all units of just one faction? Sorry, you´ll have to buy some DLC, for a completly different faction you might not even be interested in. The DLCs are spread over 3 games aswell, which makes this a headache of stupid proportions.

Only saving grace are the mods.

At it's current state it's really boring and unbalanced.
The AI attacks only unwalled settlements which makes it a cat and mouse chase game, since CA in it's infinite wisdom removed minor settlements walls.
The AI also goes out of it's way to go around your armies, and not attacking them.(Total Chase: Warhammer 3)
The AI's AntiPlayer Bias is outright silly, and makes you run around putting out fires which removes the grand strategy layer or at least reduce it significally.
The Vassal system and Alliance system is broken. 
As soon as you ally or subjucate a faction, they become totally braindead.
The AI cheats is also out of whack!

In it's state i will not recommend the game, it's broken and unbalanced.
I really used to love this series, but it needs alot of fixes AI and campaign wise!
